change.cause: The arbitrary 2048-byte prolog sample was decoded with strict EOF semantics, rejecting valid multibyte characters or surrogate pairs cut by that sample boundary.
change.repair: Use a strict incremental decoder. Decode the original prolog sample with final=false, continue strict validation over all remaining bytes in 64 KiB pieces without retaining a second full Unicode document, and finalize at the actual EOF.
retained_guards: Full-buffer byte-level DTD and entity declaration scan before decoding or parsing
Same byte buffer validation before generic Reader decoding
Strict malformed encoding and true EOF truncation rejection
change.shared_impact: The existing OOXML gate also uses validate_xml_bytes. A small stored-ZIP XML-member regression confirms valid boundary content is accepted and unsafe DTD content is rejected.

test_environment.fixture_scope: Synthetic temporary source roots and small in-memory ZIP only

runs.target: Permanent suite with three new boundary methods and expanded mixed corpus, before production repair
observations: Valid UTF-8 BOM and UTF-16 surrogate boundary inputs raised ooxml_xml_encoding_invalid.
The mixed pipeline classified two valid boundary neighbors as failed.
Invalid code units after the old sample were not checked by the former gate. The repair explicitly validates them rather than ignoring decode errors.
